newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's property tax revenues rise in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's property tax revenues rise in 1996.

text.p: Lebanese government revenues from taxation of property deals rose 31 percent to $180.58 million in 1996 over 1995, the finance ministry said on Wednesday.
The ministry collected $180.58 million at the end of 1996 compared with $137.74 million a year earlier, it said in a statement.
"The rise in tax this year came from increased selling deals and other property deals," the ministry added.

Tax rates on property deals vary from district to district but average about 6.5 percent. However, tax collection does not truly reflect the state of the market because deals are sometimes understated to avoid tax, property analysts said.
The dollar figures are based on an exchange rate of 1,552 Lebanese pounds at end of December 1996 compared with 1,596 at end of December 1995.
